description: We are a team of students from Chittagong University of Engineering & Technology (CUET) passionate about space, technology, healthcare, and innovation. For NASA Space Apps, we are developing an interactive astronaut health monitoring application that explores the effects of microgravity, radiation, isolation, sleep disruption, and other space-related factors, while providing personalized health insights
summary: ASTRA Health is an offline-first spaceflight health monitoring and clinical intelligence system designed to support astronauts and flight-medicine teams during long-duration space missions. It addresses critical healthcare challenges such as communication delays, limited medical assistance, radiation exposure, microgravity-related health changes, sleep disruption, psychological stress, and physical fatigue. Unlike conventional healthcare applications that rely on continuous internet connectivity, ASTRA ensures that essential health information and intelligence remain accessible even during communication blackouts. By integrating crew health data, physiological baselines, medical documents, NASA datasets and APIs, radiation intelligence, space-weather information, and space-life-science research, the system provides a unified platform for monitoring health, analyzing medical information, and supporting clinical decisions. Its offline AI capabilities enable astronauts to access intelligent health assistance independently of Earth-based support. Ultimately, ASTRA aims to make space healthcare more reliable, intelligent, and accessible, ensuring that astronauts can maintain their physical and psychological wellbeing throughout deep-space exploration.
details:
ASTRA Health — Astronaut Health Intelligence System

1. Project Overview

ASTRA Health is an offline-first spaceflight health monitoring and clinical intelligence system designed for astronauts, deep-space crews, and flight-medicine teams. It helps crews monitor their physical and psychological wellbeing, understand health changes, analyze medical information, and access NASA space-health intelligence even when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.

ASTRA is built around a simple idea:

Deep-space healthcare cannot depend on Earth always being one click away.

The system combines crew health data, physiological baselines, medical documents, NASA datasets and APIs, radiation intelligence, space-weather information, space-life-science research, and offline AI into one integrated platform.

2. Core Problem

During long-duration missions to the Moon, Mars, or beyond, astronauts may experience:

- Communication delays with Earth

- Temporary communication blackouts

- Limited access to medical specialists

- Radiation exposure

- Microgravity-related physiological changes

- Sleep and circadian disruption

- Psychological stress

- Physical fatigue and recovery issues

- Large amounts of medical and mission data

A conventional healthcare application that depends completely on cloud services or continuous communication may become unreliable in these situations.

ASTRA addresses this problem by making essential health intelligence available locally, offline, and continuously.

3. How ASTRA Works

ASTRA follows an offline-first workflow:

Crew Health Data → Local Storage → Health Analysis → Baseline Comparison → Clinical Document Analysis → NASA Data → AI-Assisted Intelligence → Health Insights

When connectivity is available, ASTRA can access NASA APIs and online AI services.

When connectivity is lost, the application continues using locally stored health information, mission knowledge, datasets, deterministic health rules, and an on-device AI system.

This means the application does not simply stop working when the network disappears.

4. Health Monitoring

ASTRA allows astronauts to record important health indicators such as:

- Heart rate

- Blood pressure

- SpO₂

- Exercise duration

- Physical recovery

- Sleep

- Mood

- Stress

- Energy

- Fatigue

- Daily notes

- Health check-ins

The application stores these measurements locally using IndexedDB/Dexie.js.

ASTRA can then compare new measurements against the crew member's personal baseline rather than relying only on generic population thresholds.

For example, if an astronaut's current heart rate or recovery pattern is significantly different from their normal baseline, ASTRA can highlight that change for further attention.

5. Interactive Body Health Visualization

ASTRA includes an interactive whole-body health visualization.

The visualization connects actual collected health information to corresponding areas of the body.

For example:

- Cardiovascular-related information → heart/body region

- Respiratory-related information → lungs/chest region

- Musculoskeletal information → relevant body regions

- Cognitive or psychological information → brain/mind-related region

Only health indicators that are actually collected or supported by the application are represented.

The system does not invent additional medical signals.

When the user selects a body region, ASTRA can display the corresponding health index and available information.

6. Radiation Intelligence

Radiation is one of the major health risks during deep-space missions.

ASTRA integrates NASA radiation-related information, including NASA OSDR RadLab data and calibrated MSL-RAD fallback information.

The radiation system can provide information such as:

- Absorbed dose

- Dose equivalent

- Particle-related measurements

- Radiation trends

- Radiation-risk context

This information can be connected to the astronaut health intelligence layer so that radiation is treated as part of the overall mission-health picture rather than as an isolated dashboard.

7. Space-Weather Intelligence

ASTRA also integrates NASA's DONKI — Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information.

It can monitor events such as:

- Coronal Mass Ejections

- Solar flares

- Solar energetic particles

- Geomagnetic storms

- Other space-weather notifications

These events are important because solar activity can influence radiation exposure and mission conditions.

ASTRA therefore connects external space-weather information with the crew-health context.

8. NASA Research Integration

ASTRA does not use NASA APIs simply as decorative references.

NASA information is integrated into the application's intelligence ecosystem.

ASTRA uses NASA OSDR Biological Data Repository information for space-life-science research related to areas such as:

- Cardiovascular changes

- Bone and muscle health

- Sleep

- Circadian rhythm

- Radiation

- Immune response

- Cognition

- Exercise

- Behavioral health

ASTRA can use this research as supporting evidence when interpreting mission-health questions.

9. NASA Technical Reports

ASTRA also integrates information from the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS).

NTRS provides technical and scientific references related to topics such as:

- Astronaut exercise countermeasures

- ARED and CEVIS exercise systems

- Environmental control and life-support systems

- Air and water quality

- Spaceflight health and engineering research

This gives ASTRA access to authoritative technical documentation that can strengthen its health and mission intelligence.

---

10. NASA Space Data Search

ASTRA includes a NASA-oriented search and data exploration section.

It can connect with multiple NASA data sources, including:

- NASA APOD

- NASA NeoWs/CNEOS

- NASA DONKI

- NASA OSDR

- NASA NTRS

- NASA FIRMS

- NASA EONET

- NASA climate information

- NASA Biological and Physical Sciences resources

This allows users to explore different categories of NASA information from inside the ASTRA environment.

11. Clinical Intelligence

ASTRA allows users to upload medical and laboratory documents.

The application can process documents using browser-based technologies such as:

- PDF.js

- Tesseract OCR

The system can extract available medical information such as:

- Vital signs

- Laboratory values

- Medical measurements

- Report information

The extracted information can then be incorporated into the astronaut's health context.

This helps transform static medical documents into structured health information that can be reviewed alongside other mission-health data.

---

12. Personal Health Baseline

One of ASTRA's important concepts is personalized baseline intelligence.

Instead of asking only:

«"Is this value normal for an average person?"»

ASTRA can also ask:

«"How different is this astronaut's current state from their own normal pattern?"»

The system can maintain historical information and identify changes across time.

This can make the monitoring process more personalized and useful for long-duration missions.

---

13. Offline AI

ASTRA includes an offline AI architecture designed for situations where communication with Earth is unavailable.

The offline AI is designed around a user-controlled Install / Initialize Model workflow.

The model is not automatically downloaded without user consent.

The system can use browser-based WebGPU or WASM capabilities to run AI locally.

The current architecture uses a lightweight model approach such as Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4 to keep the system practical for local execution.

The offline AI can assist with:

- Explaining health information

- Summarizing records

- Interpreting mission context

- Searching local mission knowledge

- Explaining NASA research

- Providing contextual health information

Critical medical alerts and deterministic health calculations should remain controlled by explicit rules and validated logic rather than being decided by the language model.

14. Mission Knowledge Base

ASTRA includes a curated mission knowledge base containing information relevant to astronaut health and spaceflight.

Examples include:

- Circadian rhythm

- Microgravity cardiovascular changes

- Radiation-health context

- Exercise countermeasures

- Mission-health protocols

This knowledge can remain available locally so that important information is still accessible during communication blackouts.

15. Local Mission Datasets

ASTRA also contains local seed/simulated datasets for testing and demonstrating the application.

These can include:

- Crew profiles

- Simulated telemetry

- Activity records

- Exercise information

- Sleep information

- Cognitive-test protocols

- Mission reflections

These datasets allow ASTRA to demonstrate offline operation immediately.

They should be clearly identified as simulated or seed data, not presented as real astronaut telemetry.

---

16. Online + Offline Architecture

ASTRA follows a hybrid architecture.

When Online

ASTRA can use:

- NASA APIs

- NASA datasets

- Online Gemini AI

- External research resources

- Live space-weather information

When Offline

ASTRA can continue using:

- Local health records

- IndexedDB/Dexie storage

- Personal baselines

- Local mission knowledge

- Cached NASA information

- Deterministic health rules

- Offline AI

- Local medical documents

This creates a resilient health-information system for deep-space environments.

---

17. Security Architecture

ASTRA also considers the security of health and mission information.

Important security mechanisms include:

- Server-side AI API access

- Environment-based secrets

- JWT authentication

- Google OAuth support

- Token revocation

- SHA-256 token denylisting

- Secure backend API gateway

- Client/server separation

- Local data storage controls

The Gemini API key is not intended to be exposed directly inside the client-side application.

---

18. Technology Stack

ASTRA is built using modern web technologies.

Frontend

- React

- TypeScript

- Vite

- HTML/CSS

- GSAP

- 3D/interactive UI components

Backend

- Node.js

- Express

- Server-side API proxying

Local Storage

- IndexedDB

- Dexie.js

AI

- Gemini through a secure backend gateway

- Browser-based offline AI

- WebGPU/WASM

Document Processing

- PDF.js

- Tesseract OCR

External Data

- NASA APIs

- NASA OSDR

- NASA DONKI

- NASA NTRS

- NASA CNEOS/NeoWs

- NASA APOD

- NASA FIRMS

- NASA EONET

- NASA climate and biological/physical-science resources

19. Main Benefits

ASTRA provides several important benefits:

Offline Resilience

The system remains useful during communication delays and blackouts.

Personalized Monitoring

Health changes can be compared with an astronaut's own baseline.

NASA-Connected Intelligence

Real NASA datasets and APIs contribute mission-relevant information.

Clinical Document Intelligence

Medical reports can be converted into usable health information.

Radiation Awareness

Radiation and space-weather information can be connected to crew health.

AI Assistance

AI helps explain and summarize information without replacing deterministic safety logic.

Integrated Mission Context

Health, NASA science, space weather, radiation, medical documents, and mission knowledge can be viewed together.

---

20. What Makes ASTRA Creative

ASTRA is not simply a chatbot.

It is not simply a health dashboard.

It is not simply a NASA data viewer.

Its core innovation is the combination of:

Astronaut Health + NASA Data + Offline AI + Clinical Documents + Personal Baselines + Radiation Intelligence + Space Weather + Mission Research

into one offline-first system.

The application is designed around the reality that future astronauts may have to make sense of important health information while Earth is temporarily unreachable.

---

21. Overall Architecture

The overall ASTRA architecture can be understood as:

Astronaut

↓

Health & Medical Data

↓

Local IndexedDB / Mission Storage

↓

Health Analysis + Personal Baselines

↓

Clinical Document Processing

↓

NASA Data & APIs

- RadLab

- DONKI

- OSDR

- NTRS

- CNEOS

- APOD

- FIRMS

- EONET

↓

Offline / Online AI Intelligence

↓

Health Intelligence Dashboard

↓

Crew / Flight-Medicine Team

This creates a continuous information loop between the astronaut's own health data, mission information, NASA science, and AI-assisted interpretation.

22. Core Vision

ASTRA Health is designed around one central vision:

Bring essential health intelligence closer to the crew when Earth is out of reach.

During deep-space missions, healthcare cannot always wait for a response from Earth.

ASTRA aims to provide astronauts with a resilient, personalized, NASA-connected health intelligence system that continues working online or offline.
